ass_001: You can recognise it by its wide, low crown held together with metal anchors, and a large cavity on the side facing the path. It stands on the Overcingel estate grounds off Oostersingel.
ass_003: You can recognise it by its crown, dying back and wounded on the north side while the south side still holds healthy leaves. It stands by the pond, near the Hertenkamp's 1875 stable.
ass_004: You can recognise it by its thick trunk, girthed past four metres, and its clear, uncrowded crown. It stands in Valkenstijn park, in what is now Assen-Oost.
ass_005: You can recognise it by the way it leans out over Beilerstraat from private grounds, with some dieback at the crown tips. It stands opposite house number 5, on the grounds of Nassaulaan 1.
ass_007: You can recognise it by its broken-off main trunk, now rebuilding a crown from the regrowth beneath the break. It stands on the Overcingel estate grounds, beside the horse chestnut and oak.
ass_008: You can recognise it by its dark purple-red leaves, turning copper through October. It stands in the pocket garden reached via the footpath between Alteveerstraat 59 and 61, past the weeping beech.
ass_009: You can recognise it by the two stone gateposts still standing beside it, the last remains of an old driveway. It stands at the waterside along Beilerstraat, on the former hospital grounds.
